chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding one who freed a 'sā'ibah (a slave freed on condition of serving a specific master) that there is no 'walā' (patronage) for his former masters upon him. If he wishes, he may attach himself to one of the Muslims, and he should bear witness that he guarantees his debt and every incident that binds him. If he does that, he inherits him; and if he does not do that, his inheritance is returned to the Imam of the Muslims.

key_terms.إِمَامُ الْمُُسْلِمِينَ: The Imam of the Muslims, referring to the ruling authority
key_terms.سَائِبَة: A slave freed on the condition of serving a specific master or group
key_terms.وَلَاء: Patronage or manumission bond, granting inheritance rights

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for a sā'ibah (freed slave) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) clarifies the inheritance dynamics of a 'sā'ibah', a slave manumitted conditionally, ensuring that former masters do not automatically inherit unless the freed slave explicitly attaches himself to a new patron who guarantees his liabilities. This mechanism highlights the Shia legal principle of voluntary patronage (wilayah) and the Imam's role as the ultimate heir in the absence of a valid, guaranteed patron, reflecting the structured social welfare system of the early Islamic community. The emphasis on guaranteeing 'jarirah' (liabilities) underscores the importance of financial responsibility in establishing legal kinship rights.
